props.text:
Asset Level Safety Assessment Plan

Understanding Astellas’ approach to proactive safety surveillance.

When we develop a new drug, multiple clinical trials often run at the same time. Each trial monitors safety carefully within its own protocol. However, safety data accumulates across trials, and without a systematic way to review the full picture, important patterns may be missed until late in development.

ALSAP was created to address this gap.

cards.title: A Plan
cards.content: A documented strategy that defines when and how aggregate safety data will be analyzed for a specific asset.

cards.title: A Team
cards.content: Dedicated statistical programmers and statisticians responsible for conducting the analyses.

cards.title: A Process
cards.content: Standardized procedures that connect planning, execution, and decision-making.

props.text: ALSAP Compared to Other Safety Processes

ALSAP provides proactive, planned analysis of aggregate safety data across trials. Trial-level monitoring focuses on individual studies. The Safety Management Team provides governance and decision-making, while the Safety Assessment Committee conducts unblinded reviews when required.

Each process plays a distinct role in Astellas’ overall safety strategy.

props.question: What is the primary purpose of ALSAP?
choices: To replace the Safety Management Team
To provide real-time monitoring within individual trials
To systematically analyze aggregate safety data across trials

feedback.correct: That’s right. ALSAP provides proactive, systematic analysis of aggregate safety data across trials.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. ALSAP focuses on aggregate analysis across trials, not replacing existing governance or trial-level monitoring.

cards.title: Plan
cards.content: The asset team determines ALSAP is needed and drafts an ALSAP Plan.

cards.title: Assign
cards.content: A dedicated ALSAP programmer or statistician is assigned.

cards.title: Execute
cards.content: Aggregate safety analyses are performed according to the plan.

cards.title: Review
cards.content: The SMT reviews outputs and assesses potential safety signals.

cards.title: Act
cards.content: Findings are documented, escalated if needed, and actions are implemented.

scenes.title: Why ALSAP May Matter to You

props.text: When Might ALSAP Affect Your Work?

ALSAP connects to many roles across the organization. Clinical Operations may support data access. Drug Safety may use ALSAP findings for signal detection. Regulatory Affairs may reference ALSAP outputs in submissions. Biostatistics and programming teams may collaborate on analyses. SMT members review ALSAP outputs and determine next steps.

props.question: When might ALSAP be particularly useful?
choices: When waiting for all trials to complete
When similar safety findings appear across multiple trials
When monitoring a single trial only

feedback.correct: Correct. ALSAP helps identify patterns across multiple trials.
feedback.incorrect: ALSAP is most useful when looking across trials, not within a single study.

props.text: Key documents include the ALSAP SOP and the ALSAP Plan template. If you have questions about ALSAP or how it may relate to your work, reach out to the ALSAP team or your project lead. Additional role-specific training is available for ALSAP team members, SMT members, and Asset Leads.
